bull_bear.body:
- Pan-India distribution and service network built on Authorized Business Partners (ABPs) and sub-dealers, with Indef Clinics providing specialized after-sales support
- Regional sales offices in Delhi, Chennai and Kolkata plus regional sales engineers for deeper market penetration
- Brand equity drawn from the 97-year Bajaj Group legacy, reinforced by a 2023 rebranding to 'Bajaj Indef'
- Multi-brand portfolio (Bajaj Indef, SWIFT, Daedalus) spanning price points from large enterprises to price-sensitive MSMEs
- Growing export network of sales engineers and ABPs across the Middle East and Africa (MEA) region
- Market-leading position in hoisting solutions across India, per the Directors' Report
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity price risk on raw materials — Basic input ingredients are various grades of steel and copper, whose prices are volatile; the company sources components directly from vendors and does not hedge this exposure, relying instead on its ability to pass on substantial price hikes to customers.
- Geopolitical and global trade disruption — FY 2025-26 operating environment was challenged by heightened geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, continued disruptions to global shipping routes, and evolving global trade dynamics, contributing to volatility in commodity and energy prices, higher freight costs, and supply chain uncertainty, which led to a cautious capex approach in certain industrial sectors served by the company.
- Dependence on the industrial capex cycle — Business is closely linked to the investment cycle in new projects, industrial capacity expansions, and overall sentiment across the manufacturing and infrastructure sectors, making demand sensitive to broader capex trends among customer industries.
- Credit risk on trade receivables — Trade receivables are typically unsecured, exposing the company to counterparty default risk; managed through credit approvals, credit limits and continuous monitoring of customer creditworthiness.
- Reduced dedicated risk-oversight structure — A proposal to dissolve the Risk Management Committee (constituted in September 2024, not mandatorily required at the company's current size under SEBI LODR) was placed before the Board on May 25, 2026; if approved, risk-management oversight would shift to be undertaken directly by the Board rather than a dedicated committee.
- Unhedged foreign currency exposure on imports — The company imports certain materials and does not currently hedge this foreign currency exposure, though the value is presently insignificant relative to total raw material consumption; it may enter hedging arrangements in future depending on import volumes and market conditions.
- Market risk on treasury investments — Surplus funds invested in mutual funds and fixed deposits expose the company to security price risk, mitigated through portfolio diversification.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Indef Manufacturing Limited manufactures, sells, distributes and markets mechanical hoists (chain pulley blocks, ratchet lever hoists), electric chain and wire rope hoists, EOT/gantry/jib/light profile cranes, and floor-operated stackers and roll-out racks for storage and retrieval. It serves large corporations, EPC contractors and MSMEs across automotive, energy, infrastructure, engineering, metals, steel, cement, chemicals, logistics, textiles and food processing, through a pan-India network of Authorized Business Partners (ABPs) and sub-dealers plus a growing export footprint in the Middle East and Africa.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Mechanical Hoists:** Chain pulley blocks, Ratchet lever hoists
- **Electric Hoists:** Electric chain hoists, Electric wire rope hoists, CRH Wire Rope Hoist, Glacier
- **Cranes:** EOT (electric overhead travelling) cranes, Gantry cranes, Jib cranes, Light profile cranes
- **Storage & Retrieval:** Floor-operated stackers, Roll-out racks
- **Specialised:** Transfer Trolley, Stainless Steel Chain Pulley Block for clean room applications, Manipulators and material handling automation solutions
- **Brands:** Bajaj Indef, iCrane, iStacker, SWIFT, Daedalus by Bajaj Indef
business.title: Products & brands

business.body:
- Consolidated Swift Industries Limited — subsidiary: 100% wholly-owned subsidiary since September 6, 2024 (SWIFT brand); Amit Bhalla is a Director.
- Daedalus Lift & Access Equipments Private Limited — subsidiary: 80% equity stake acquired September 9, 2025, operating as 'Daedalus by Bajaj Indef' in the Aerial Working Platform segment; Amit Bhalla is a Director.
- Hercules Investment Limited — related party: Predecessor entity (formerly Hercules Hoists Limited) from which the material handling business was demerged. Shekhar Bajaj is Chairman and Director; Girija Balakrishnan and Jayavanth Kallianpur Mallya are Directors; Shekhar Bajaj and his brother Niraj Bajaj each hold more than 2% of paid-up share capital.
- Bajaj Electricals Limited — related party: Shekhar Bajaj, Pooja Bajaj (daughter-in-law of Shekhar Bajaj) and Vikram Taranath Hosangady are Directors; Shekhar Bajaj holds more than 2% of paid-up share capital.
- Bajaj International Pvt. Ltd. — related party: Shekhar Bajaj is Chairman and Director; Niraj Bajaj (brother of Shekhar Bajaj) is a Member.
- BAJEL Projects Ltd. — related party: Shekhar Bajaj is Chairman and Director, and holds more than 2% of paid-up share capital.
- Mukand Limited — related party: Niraj Bajaj, brother of Shekhar Bajaj, is Director and holds more than 2% of paid-up share capital.
- Mukund Sumi Special Steel Limited — related party: Niraj Bajaj, brother of Shekhar Bajaj, is Director.
- Bajaj General Insurance Ltd. — related party: Niraj Bajaj, brother of Shekhar Bajaj, is Director.
- Hind Musafir Agency Ltd. — related party: Shekhar Bajaj is Director and holds more than 2% of paid-up share capital.
- Hindustan Housing Co. Ltd. — related party: Shekhar Bajaj holds more than 2% of paid-up share capital; Jayavanth Kallianpur Mallya is Director.
business.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)

business.body:
- Pan-India distribution and service network built on Authorized Business Partners (ABPs) and sub-dealers, with Indef Clinics providing specialized after-sales support
- Regional sales offices in Delhi, Chennai and Kolkata plus regional sales engineers for deeper market penetration
- Brand equity drawn from the 97-year Bajaj Group legacy, reinforced by a 2023 rebranding to 'Bajaj Indef'
- Multi-brand portfolio (Bajaj Indef, SWIFT, Daedalus) spanning price points from large enterprises to price-sensitive MSMEs
- Growing export network of sales engineers and ABPs across the Middle East and Africa (MEA) region
- Market-leading position in hoisting solutions across India, per the Directors' Report
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Strengthen market competitiveness through improved supply chain efficiency, cost optimization, and continuous product portfolio refinement.
- Deepen presence across India while actively strengthening global reach through targeted export initiatives and strategic partnerships, scaling footprint across the Middle East and Africa and other priority geographies.
- Accelerate scale-up of subsidiary businesses SWIFT and Daedalus as independent growth engines addressing distinct customer segments and price points, leveraging the broader Bajaj Indef ecosystem's trust and reach.
- Continue investing in expanding product offerings, both organically and through collaborations, to address evolving customer needs across industry segments and geographies.
- Sharpen focus on penetrating new and emerging customer segments, including data centres, building dedicated go-to-market strategies to capture demand from digital infrastructure build-out.
- Accelerate digitization of business data, workflows and service processes, integrating AI- and ML-driven analytics to enhance decision-making, demand forecasting and internal operations.
- Build future-ready workforce capabilities under Project Saksham, a structured learning and development initiative for capability-building across the organization.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Growth during FY 2025-26 was driven primarily by portfolio and brand expansion rather than new plant capacity: the company completed acquisition of an 80% equity stake in Daedalus Lift & Access Equipments Private Limited (branded 'Daedalus by Bajaj Indef'), marking its entry into the Aerial Working Platform (AWP) segment and meaningfully expanding the product portfolio, building on the prior-year acquisition of the SWIFT brand which addresses the price-sensitive MSME segment. The company also expanded its product range with the introduction of the Transfer Trolley, CRH Wire Rope Hoist, Glacier, and Stainless Steel Chain Pulley Block (CPB) for clean room applications, and continued to invest in advanced manufacturing technologies at its existing Khalapur and Chakan (Maharashtra) facilities and in expanding its ABP network across the Middle East and Africa region.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Business remains closely linked to the investment cycle in new projects, industrial capacity expansions, and overall sentiment across manufacturing and infrastructure sectors.
- FY 2025-26 demand from capex-intensive industries was supported by positive government signals including increased infrastructure outlays, the push for domestic manufacturing under PLI schemes, and sustained focus on logistics and supply chain modernization.
- Long-term demand expected to be driven by infrastructure development, increased manufacturing activity, logistics and warehousing expansion, automation initiatives, and continued public and private sector capital expenditure.
- Operating environment during FY 2025-26 was challenged by heightened geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, disruptions to global shipping routes, and evolving global trade dynamics, contributing to volatility in commodity and energy prices, increased freight costs, and supply chain uncertainties, leading to a cautious capex approach in certain industrial sectors.
- Despite short-term headwinds, sustained infrastructure spending and continued investments in manufacturing supported demand for material handling solutions, with the company delivering resilient revenue growth of 10.73% over the previous year.
- Real GDP grew 7.7% in FY 2025-26 (up from 7.1% previous year), driven by robust manufacturing and services activity and sustained investment, providing a favourable backdrop for the capital goods and material handling equipment industry through much of the year.
